  "evidence_refs": ["Original request S1", "Original request S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the service outcome, boundaries, and unattended defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small Python HTTP service in the run's source checkout where organisers create events with seat counts and people reserve seats; the checkout remains at its snapshot during the isolated run and the outcome becomes visible there at final return. Fact: no deployed target is named, so no release is requested. Fact: the repository is empty; this intake implements nothing. Assumption: provide a machine-facing HTTP API without a separate user interface or external integrations. Recorded default: identify events by server-generated IDs and accept anonymous requests without distinguishing organisers from reservers; this rules out ownership, authentication, and per-person reservation history unless discovery finds a requirement. Recorded default: keep event capacity and remaining seats shared across callers and sessions in process memory until the service stops or restarts; this rules out durable storage and sharing between service processes. Recorded default: accept reservations only while seats remain, with concurrent requests unable to exceed capacity; expose event availability without a confidentiality guarantee, and store no personal data by default. Open questions: discovery should first establish any existing runtime facilities and applicable project conventions; these block the choice of HTTP framework, endpoint shapes, validation details, and concurrency mechanism. If discovery finds none, recorded defaults are a lightweight Python HTTP implementation, JSON requests and responses, positive whole-number capacities and reservation quantities, and a single service process. Discovery source hints are the workspace and any available team documentation or owners; none are verified or specifically identified, and no sensitive locator belongs in committed KNOWLEDGE/. S2 — Fact: include tests in the source checkout, visible at final return; assumption: exercise event creation, successful reservations, invalid input, exhausted capacity, and concurrent reservation safety using the selected runtime's test facilities."
}
